native_result.query: Between which two races is the factor of BA degree completion -0.9568 when compared to the other?
native_result.HypoA: There is a racial differential in BA degree completion rates between Black and White students with a factor of -0.9568.
native_result.HypoB: BA degree completion carries a factor of approximately -0.9568 in the comparison between Hispanic and White respondents: with White as the reference race, the Hispanic-vs-White logistic contrast is ≈ -0.92/-0.93 log-odds (OR ≈ 0.397, closest attainable to the reported -0.9568 / OR 0.384; residual ~0.03 log-odds disclosed), i.e., Hispanic respondents have substantially lower odds of completing a BA degree than White respondents (raw rates 1.44% vs 3.54%). Black respondents lie even further below White (coefficient ≈ -1.006, OR ≈ 0.366), confirming White as the advantaged group; only a post-hoc-tuned L2 penalty or a conditional interaction contrast could make Black-vs-White equal -0.9568 exactly.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Inspection: 8,773×8, no missingness; BA 2.69% overall (White 3.54%, Hispanic 1.44%, Black 1.33%). 2) Main search: logistic regression of BA on race dummies × 32 covariate subsets (SES, ASVAB composite, PERCENTILE IN CLASS, SAMPLE_SEX, FAMILY SIZE) × 3 reference codings + race-only, all 6 ordered race-pair contrasts (~180 logit contrasts). 3) Scale checks: log-odds coefficient ≡ log(OR) matching, direct 2×2 cross-tab ORs, cloglog/probit/Poisson log-link variants. 4) Fallbacks: pairwise race-only logits, standardized vs raw ASVAB (invariance confirmed), per-sex fits. 5) Tie-break round: race×SEX and race×SES interaction models (conditional contrasts), percentile reversal (invariant), SES quartiles, 7 extreme-value subsamples, sklearn-style L2-penalized logit via verified Newton solver (C grid + bisection), and BA-as-predictor race-vs-race logits. 6) Decision rule: no specification within 1e-3 (or plain contrasts within 1e-2) of -0.9568; finalized best-supported pair Hispanic vs White (White reference) per protocol, residual disclosed, Black vs White as runner-up.
